reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of conformal time series prediction lies in decoupling the static nature of traditional prediction intervals from the evolving dynamics of real-world data. Vision Prediction Sets (VPS) provide a mechanism for constructing prediction sets that maintain coverage guarantees regardless of whether the data is exchangeable or adversarially generated. This is achieved by treating the construction of prediction sets as a sequential decision-making process rather than a fixed statistical procedure. Conformal PID Control extends this idea by framing the calibration of these sets as a control problem, where the quantile level is adjusted adaptively based on observed miscoverage. The controller uses a proportional feedback mechanism to track desired coverage rates, making it robust against distributional shifts. In GSI, this translates into maintaining reliable uncertainty quantification across varying game conditions, while in GSE, it enables a hybrid forecasting system that switches between standard conformal intervals and adaptive controllers during regime changes. The failure mode occurs when the underlying assumptions about the stability of the environment are violated beyond the controller’s capacity to adapt, leading to degraded coverage performance.
